question.problem:
Let $u=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 9 \\ 3t \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}t \\ 2 \\ -5 \\ {t}^{2} \\ 5\end{aligned}].$
If $u\cdot v=-2$ and $t>3$, find the value of $t.$
question.worked_solution:
Starting from the equation $u\cdot v=-2,$ we compute the dot product in terms of $t$ and then solve for $t$ in the resulting equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & =-2 \\ 7\cdot t+9\cdot 2+3t\cdot (-5)+1\cdot {t}^{2}+(-1)\cdot 5 & =-2 \\ 7t+18-15t+{t}^{2}-5 & =-2 \\ {t}^{2}-8t+15 & =0 \\ (t-3)(t-5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We get two solutions, ${t}_{1}=3$ and ${t}_{2}=5.$ Since we need $t>3$, our final answer is $t=5$ only.
